=== #1988
## Context

While regenerating `frontend/a11y-baseline.json` for #1981 (the useId→ancestry keying fix, review finding 1), the `run detail` case in `frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` produced a DIFFERENT gated-violation count depending on how it was invoked:

- Run standalone, or preceded only by the `results` test (`playwright test e2e/a11y.spec.ts -g "results|run detail"`): **13** serious/critical violations, stable across 3 repeats.
- Run as part of the full 8-test spec file (`dashboard` → `connections` → `suites list` → `suite detail` → `results` → `run detail` → `assets` → `admin`, the sequence CI and `pnpm a11y:baseline` both use): **0** violations, stable across repeated full-suite runs.

Each test gets its own fresh Playwright page/context (no shared storage), so this isn't a stale-session issue. The likely cause: the Results table's "first row" (`page.locator('tr.ant-table-row').first()`) resolves to a *different seeded run* depending on how much wall-clock time/backend state has passed before the `run detail` test executes, and only some runs' detail pages render a muted `ant-typography-secondary` caption that fails `color-contrast`. That capping element differs per run's data.

## Impact

The committed baseline for `route:/results/:id` (currently **0** rows, reflecting the deterministic-in-CI full-suite sequence) is only correct for that exact invocation order. A future `pnpm a11y:baseline` regen run that inserts, removes, or reorders a test in `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` — or one run manually with a subset of tests (`-g`) — will likely see a nonzero count for this surface again and could file it as a "new violation" when it's actually the same underlying issue reappearing.

## Suggested fix

Pick the run-detail target deterministically instead of "first row in whatever order the table currently renders" — e.g. click a row identified by suite/check name, or add an explicit `ORDER BY` tie-break to the `runs` list endpoint so `least-recently-inserted`/`id` decides ties instead of relying on `started_at` (which the demo seed can produce with duplicate values). Re-verify with the same standalone-vs-full-suite comparison this issue used to find the bug.

Filed per CONTRIBUTING rule 3a — found live, verified real (not test noise), deferred because it's outside the scope of #1981's three review findings.

=== #1671
Item 2 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan — highest user-impact single item. Severity is communicated almost entirely by color today (red/orange/green tags, recharts series where color is the ONLY encoding). Add icons/shapes/text beside color everywhere severity or status renders, and adopt a colorblind-safe palette. ~8% of male users can't reliably read the current severity language. Includes the dashboards' chart series. Reduced-motion support rides along per the plan's item 5 (cheap here).

=== #1672
Item 3 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: full keyboard traversal of the screen set; focus-trap + restore on the surviving drawers/modals (Share, version history, run progress, import); visible focus states; skip-to-content. antd gives a decent baseline — the custom drawer/table/editor compositions are where it breaks. Verify in a real browser (the jsdom-proves-nothing lesson, #1282).

=== #1673
Item 4 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: landmarks; headers/captions on the results/runs tables; aria-live for async run-progress updates; and a text alternative for every chart — the dashboards are pure-visual today. A data-table fallback per chart covers both a11y and the PDF-export path (#345 shipped as #1122). New code stops hard-coding user-facing strings now (i18n stays deferred, but don't make it worse — plan item 5).

1. **`color-contrast` on `.ant-typography-secondary`** (86 of 107) — a theme-token change, likely one PR, likely folds into [#1671](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1671)'s colorblind-safe palette work rather than a separate pass.
2. **`label` on filter `Select`s** (17) — associate the visible label text via `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on the antd `Select`'s underlying input; concentrated on Results and Suites.

The baseline was captured against the CI-equivalent stack (Postgres+Redis+OpenBao, migrated + seeded, uvicorn dev-bypass API, Vite) plus the OTP stack for the sign-in route, and is stable across repeated captures (the raw axe selector for a couple of `Select` instances turned out to be flaky — a React `useId()`-minted id that isn't stable across page loads — so the ratchet's selector-matching normalizes those out before comparing; see `frontend/scripts/a11y/ratchet.ts`).

=== #1988
## Context

While regenerating `frontend/a11y-baseline.json` for #1981 (the useId→ancestry keying fix, review finding 1), the `run detail` case in `frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` produced a DIFFERENT gated-violation count depending on how it was invoked:

- Run standalone, or preceded only by the `results` test (`playwright test e2e/a11y.spec.ts -g "results|run detail"`): **13** serious/critical violations, stable across 3 repeats.
- Run as part of the full 8-test spec file (`dashboard` → `connections` → `suites list` → `suite detail` → `results` → `run detail` → `assets` → `admin`, the sequence CI and `pnpm a11y:baseline` both use): **0** violations, stable across repeated full-suite runs.

Each test gets its own fresh Playwright page/context (no shared storage), so this isn't a stale-session issue. The likely cause: the Results table's "first row" (`page.locator('tr.ant-table-row').first()`) resolves to a *different seeded run* depending on how much wall-clock time/backend state has passed before the `run detail` test executes, and only some runs' detail pages render a muted `ant-typography-secondary` caption that fails `color-contrast`. That capping element differs per run's data.

## Impact

The committed baseline for `route:/results/:id` (currently **0** rows, reflecting the deterministic-in-CI full-suite sequence) is only correct for that exact invocation order. A future `pnpm a11y:baseline` regen run that inserts, removes, or reorders a test in `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` — or one run manually with a subset of tests (`-g`) — will likely see a nonzero count for this surface again and could file it as a "new violation" when it's actually the same underlying issue reappearing.

## Suggested fix

Pick the run-detail target deterministically instead of "first row in whatever order the table currently renders" — e.g. click a row identified by suite/check name, or add an explicit `ORDER BY` tie-break to the `runs` list endpoint so `least-recently-inserted`/`id` decides ties instead of relying on `started_at` (which the demo seed can produce with duplicate values). Re-verify with the same standalone-vs-full-suite comparison this issue used to find the bug.

Filed per CONTRIBUTING rule 3a — found live, verified real (not test noise), deferred because it's outside the scope of #1981's three review findings.

=== #1671
Item 2 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan — highest user-impact single item. Severity is communicated almost entirely by color today (red/orange/green tags, recharts series where color is the ONLY encoding). Add icons/shapes/text beside color everywhere severity or status renders, and adopt a colorblind-safe palette. ~8% of male users can't reliably read the current severity language. Includes the dashboards' chart series. Reduced-motion support rides along per the plan's item 5 (cheap here).

=== #1672
Item 3 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: full keyboard traversal of the screen set; focus-trap + restore on the surviving drawers/modals (Share, version history, run progress, import); visible focus states; skip-to-content. antd gives a decent baseline — the custom drawer/table/editor compositions are where it breaks. Verify in a real browser (the jsdom-proves-nothing lesson, #1282).

=== #1673
Item 4 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: landmarks; headers/captions on the results/runs tables; aria-live for async run-progress updates; and a text alternative for every chart — the dashboards are pure-visual today. A data-table fallback per chart covers both a11y and the PDF-export path (#345 shipped as #1122). New code stops hard-coding user-facing strings now (i18n stays deferred, but don't make it worse — plan item 5).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Scratch stack for the docs screenshot/video lane (frontend/e2e-docs/).
# Mirrors CI's frontend-e2e job — dev-bypass auth, seeded demo data — on its
# own database, OpenBao KV mount and ports, so the developer's compose stack
# (and its orphan-secret sweep) never sees it. Reuses the compose Postgres
# (:5432), Redis (:6379, db 3) and OpenBao (:8200).
#
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh start    # migrate + seed + api :8001 + vite :3001
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh capture  # run the e2e-docs Playwright project
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh stop     # stop the processes (data kept)
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh destroy  # stop + drop the database + the KV mount
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
RUN="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dataq-docs-capture"
mkdir -p "$RUN"
API_PORT="${DOCS_API_PORT:-8001}"
WEB_PORT="${DOCS_WEB_PORT:-3001}"
DB_NAME="${DOCS_DB_NAME:-dataq_docs}"
KV_MOUNT="${DOCS_KV_MOUNT:-docs-capture}"
COMPOSE=(docker compose -f "$ROOT/docker-compose.yml")

_env() {
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$ROOT/.env"
  set +a
  export DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
  export REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/3"
  export SECRET_STORE=openbao
  export OPENBAO_ADDR="http://localhost:8200"
  export OPENBAO_TOKEN
  export OPENBAO_MOUNT="$KV_MOUNT"
  export AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true
  # Explicitly NOT OTP: a developer's .env.app may configure it, and OTP wins
  # over dev-bypass at import time (core/auth.py).
  export AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS= AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS= AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST= AUTH_EMAIL_FROM=
  export DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=
  export ENVIRONMENT=dev
  export REDACTED@dataq.local
  export RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false
  export DATAQ_ROLE_TOKENS_PATH="$RUN/.role-tokens.json"
}

_alive() { [ -f "$RUN/$1.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$RUN/$1.pid")" 2>/dev/null; }

_psql() { "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d postgres -tAc "$1"; }

_bao() { curl -sf -X "$1" -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8200/v1/$2" "${@:3}"; }

start() {
  _env
  if _alive api || _alive web; then
    echo "already running (pids in $RUN) — run 'stop' first"; exit 1
  fi
  _psql "select 1 from pg_database where datname='${DB_NAME}'" | grep -q 1 \
    || _psql "create database ${DB_NAME}" >/dev/null
  _bao GET "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || _bao POST "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"type":"kv","options":{"version":"2"}}' >/dev/null
  (cd "$ROOT/backend" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output alembic upgrade head >"$RUN/alembic.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev >"$RUN/seed.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && nohup conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output \
      uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$API_PORT" >"$RUN/api.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$RUN/api.pid")
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null && break; sleep 1
  done
  curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null || { echo "api did not come up"; tail -20 "$RUN/api.log"; exit 1; }
  # The seed carries no llm_settings row; the LLM captures need a saved, enabled
  # OpenAI-compatible config so a fresh stack regenerates the same images. The
  # key is a placeholder (Ollama ignores it); Test only shows OK when a server
  # answers at DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL.
  curl -sf -o /dev/null -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/admin/llm" \
    -d "{\"provider\":\"openai_compatible\",\"model\":\"${DOCS_LLM_MODEL:-qwen2.5:14b}\",\"base_url\":\"${DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1}\",\"api_key\":\"docs-capture-placeholder\",\"structured_output\":\"prompt_json\",\"enabled\":true}" \
    || { echo "could not seed the LLM provider config"; exit 1; }
  # Optional: a real Snowflake reader connection + suite, for the SQL-generation and
  # suggest-checks captures (both need to introspect a live table — a fake config
  # errors on every call). Skipped when DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT is unset, so the base
  # capture set still works with no warehouse credentials at hand; export it (plus
  # DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER/_SECRET, the rest default to the harness reader's shape —

#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh capture  # run the e2e-docs Playwright project
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh stop     # stop the processes (data kept)
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh destroy  # stop + drop the database + the KV mount
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
RUN="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dataq-docs-capture"
mkdir -p "$RUN"
API_PORT="${DOCS_API_PORT:-8001}"
WEB_PORT="${DOCS_WEB_PORT:-3001}"
DB_NAME="${DOCS_DB_NAME:-dataq_docs}"
KV_MOUNT="${DOCS_KV_MOUNT:-docs-capture}"
COMPOSE=(docker compose -f "$ROOT/docker-compose.yml")

_env() {
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$ROOT/.env"
  set +a
  export DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
  export REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/3"
  export SECRET_STORE=openbao
  export OPENBAO_ADDR="http://localhost:8200"
  export OPENBAO_TOKEN
  export OPENBAO_MOUNT="$KV_MOUNT"
  export AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true
  # Explicitly NOT OTP: a developer's .env.app may configure it, and OTP wins
  # over dev-bypass at import time (core/auth.py).
  export AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS= AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS= AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST= AUTH_EMAIL_FROM=
  export DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=
  export ENVIRONMENT=dev
  export REDACTED@dataq.local
  export RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false
  export DATAQ_ROLE_TOKENS_PATH="$RUN/.role-tokens.json"
}

_alive() { [ -f "$RUN/$1.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$RUN/$1.pid")" 2>/dev/null; }

_psql() { "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d postgres -tAc "$1"; }

_bao() { curl -sf -X "$1" -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8200/v1/$2" "${@:3}"; }

start() {
  _env
  if _alive api || _alive web; then
    echo "already running (pids in $RUN) — run 'stop' first"; exit 1
  fi
  _psql "select 1 from pg_database where datname='${DB_NAME}'" | grep -q 1 \
    || _psql "create database ${DB_NAME}" >/dev/null
  _bao GET "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || _bao POST "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"type":"kv","options":{"version":"2"}}' >/dev/null
  (cd "$ROOT/backend" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output alembic upgrade head >"$RUN/alembic.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev >"$RUN/seed.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && nohup conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output \
      uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$API_PORT" >"$RUN/api.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$RUN/api.pid")
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null && break; sleep 1
  done
  curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null || { echo "api did not come up"; tail -20 "$RUN/api.log"; exit 1; }
  # The seed carries no llm_settings row; the LLM captures need a saved, enabled
  # OpenAI-compatible config so a fresh stack regenerates the same images. The
  # key is a placeholder (Ollama ignores it); Test only shows OK when a server
  # answers at DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL.
  curl -sf -o /dev/null -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/admin/llm" \
    -d "{\"provider\":\"openai_compatible\",\"model\":\"${DOCS_LLM_MODEL:-qwen2.5:14b}\",\"base_url\":\"${DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1}\",\"api_key\":\"docs-capture-placeholder\",\"structured_output\":\"prompt_json\",\"enabled\":true}" \
    || { echo "could not seed the LLM provider config"; exit 1; }
  # Optional: a real Snowflake reader connection + suite, for the SQL-generation and
  # suggest-checks captures (both need to introspect a live table — a fake config
  # errors on every call). Skipped when DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT is unset, so the base
  # capture set still works with no warehouse credentials at hand; export it (plus
  # DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER/_SECRET, the rest default to the harness reader's shape —

content.text:
Provide a code review for the given pull request.

To do this, follow these steps precisely:

1. Use a Haiku agent to check if the pull request (a) is closed, (b) is a draft, (c) does not need a code review (eg. because it is an automated pull request, or is very simple and obviously ok), or (d) already has a code review from you from earlier. If so, do not proceed.
2. Use another Haiku agent to give you a list of file paths to (but not the contents of) any relevant CLAUDE.md files from the codebase: the root CLAUDE.md file (if one exists), as well as any CLAUDE.md files in the directories whose files the pull request modified
3. Use a Haiku agent to view the pull request, and ask the agent to return a summary of the change
4. Then, launch 5 parallel Sonnet agents to independently code review the change. The agents should do the following, then return a list of issues and the reason each issue was flagged (eg. CLAUDE.md adherence, bug, historical git context, etc.):
   a. Agent #1: Audit the changes to make sure they compily with the CLAUDE.md. Note that CLAUDE.md is guidance for Claude as it writes code, so not all instructions will be applicable during code review.
   b. Agent #2: Read the file changes in the pull request, then do a shallow scan for obvious bugs. Avoid reading extra context beyond the changes, focusing just on the changes themselves. Focus on large bugs, and avoid small issues and nitpicks. Ignore likely false positives.
   c. Agent #3: Read the git blame and history of the code modified, to identify any bugs in light of that historical context
   d. Agent #4: Read previous pull requests that touched these files, and check for any comments on those pull requests that may also apply to the current pull request.
   e. Agent #5: Read code comments in the modified files, and make sure the changes in the pull request comply with any guidance in the comments.
5. For each issue found in #4, launch a parallel Haiku agent that takes the PR, issue description, and list of CLAUDE.md files (from step 2), and returns a score to indicate the agent's level of confidence for whether the issue is real or false positive. To do that, the agent should score each issue on a scale from 0-100, indicating its level of confidence. For issues that were flagged due to CLAUDE.md instructions, the agent should double check that the CLAUDE.md actually calls out that issue specifically. The scale is (give this rubric to the agent verbatim):
   a. 0: Not confident at all. This is a false positive that doesn't stand up to light scrutiny, or is a pre-existing issue.
   b. 25: Somewhat confident. This might be a real issue, but may also be a false positive. The agent wasn't able to verify that it's a real issue. If the issue is stylistic, it is one that was not explicitly called out in the relevant CLAUDE.md.
   c. 50: Moderately confident. The agent was able to verify this is a real issue, but it might be a nitpick or not happen very often in practice. Relative to the rest of the PR, it's not very important.
   d. 75: Highly confident. The agent double checked the issue, and verified that it is very likely it is a real issue that will be hit in practice. The existing approach in the PR is insufficient. The issue is very important and will directly impact the code's functionality, or it is an issue that is directly mentioned in the relevant CLAUDE.md.
   e. 100: Absolutely certain. The agent double checked the issue, and confirmed that it is definitely a real issue, that will happen frequently in practice. The evidence directly confirms this.
6. Filter out any issues with a score less than 80. If there are no issues that meet this criteria, do not proceed.
7. Use a Haiku agent to repeat the eligibility check from #1, to make sure that the pull request is still eligible for code review.
8. Finally, use the gh bash command to comment back on the pull request with the result. When writing your comment, keep in mind to:
   a. Keep your output brief
   b. Avoid emojis
   c. Link and cite relevant code, files, and URLs

Examples of false positives, for steps 4 and 5:

- Pre-existing issues
- Something that looks like a bug but is not actually a bug
- Pedantic nitpicks that a senior engineer wouldn't call out
- Issues that a linter, typechecker, or compiler would catch (eg. missing or incorrect imports, type errors, broken tests, formatting issues, pedantic style issues like newlines). No need to run these build steps yourself -- it is safe to assume that they will be run separately as part of CI.
- General code quality issues (eg. lack of test coverage, general security issues, poor documentation), unless explicitly required in CLAUDE.md
- Issues that are called out in CLAUDE.md, but explicitly silenced in the code (eg. due to a lint ignore comment)
- Changes in functionality that are likely intentional or are directly related to the broader change
- Real issues, but on lines that the user did not modify in their pull request

Notes:

- Do not check build signal or attempt to build or typecheck the app. These will run separately, and are not relevant to your code review.
- Use `gh` to interact with Github (eg. to fetch a pull request, or to create inline comments), rather than web fetch
- Make a todo list first
- You must cite and link each bug (eg. if referring to a CLAUDE.md, you must link it)
- For your final comment, follow the following format precisely (assuming for this example that you found 3 issues):

---

### Code review

Found 3 issues:

1. <brief description of bug> (CLAUDE.md says "<...>")

<link to file and line with full sha1 + line range for context, note that you MUST provide the full sha and not use bash here, eg. https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/1d54823877c4de72b2316a64032a54afc404e619/README.md#L13-L17>

2. <brief description of bug> (some/other/CLAUDE.md says "<...>")

<link to file and line with full sha1 + line range for context>

3. <brief description of bug> (bug due to <file and code snippet>)

<link to file and line with full sha1 + line range for context>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

<sub>- If this code review was useful, please react with 👍. Otherwise, react with 👎.</sub>

---

- Or, if you found no issues:

---

### Code review

No issues found. Checked for bugs and CLAUDE.md compliance.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

- When linking to code, follow the following format precisely, otherwise the Markdown preview won't render correctly: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-cli-internal/blob/c21d3c10bc8e898b7ac1a2d745bdc9bc4e423afe/package.json#L10-L15
  - Requires full git sha
  - You must provide the full sha. Commands like `https://github.com/owner/repo/blob/$(git rev-parse HEAD)/foo/bar` will not work, since your comment will be directly rendered in Markdown.
  - Repo name must match the repo you're code reviewing
  - # sign after the file name
  - Line range format is L[start]-L[end]
  - Provide at least 1 line of context before and after, centered on the line you are commenting about (eg. if you are commenting about lines 5-6, you should link to `L4-7`)

input.description: Review: shallow bug scan
input.prompt:
Code review of GitHub PR #2050 in repo TheurgicDuke771/DataQ (working dir /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ). READ-ONLY: do NOT run git checkout/switch/stash/reset or modify any file; use `gh pr diff 2050`. Do not build or typecheck.

PR summary: adds a shared `settle(page)` Playwright helper (frontend/scripts/a11y/settle.ts) awaited before every axe-core scan in frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts and frontend/e2e-otp/a11y.spec.ts. It (1) asserts `.ant-spin-spinning, .ant-skeleton-active` has count 0, then (2) awaits `.finished` on every `document.getAnimations()` entry whose computed timing iterations is not Infinity. Purpose: axe reports color-contrast as "incomplete" rather than a violation under a sub-opaque ancestor, and antd's Spin blurs its container to opacity 0.5, so mid-load scans passed vacuously. Also regenerates frontend/a11y-baseline.json.

Your task: read the diff and do a shallow scan for OBVIOUS, LARGE bugs in the changed lines only. Think about: can `settle` hang (e.g. a paused animation whose `finished` never resolves, an infinite animation not filtered by the iterations check, `getAnimations()` missing subtree/shadow animations), can it pass while content is still loading (loading states that are not Spin/Skeleton, e.g. antd Table `loading`, Suspense fallbacks, data arriving after Spin clears), is the `expect(...).toHaveCount(0)` racy when the spinner has not appeared YET at call time, is the import of `expect` from '@playwright/test' in a scripts/ file a problem given e2e-otp uses its own './fixtures' expect. Verify each suspicion against the actual code in the repo (read files under frontend/src as needed) before reporting. Avoid nitpicks and likely false positives; ignore anything a linter/typechecker would catch and anything on lines the PR did not modify.

Return a list of issues, each with file + line range, description, why it is a real bug, and how confident you are. If none, say "no issues".

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Bring up the backend half of the email-OTP browser lane (ADR 0032, #736).
# Starts, in order (the order is load-bearing): 1. the SMTP sink on :1025/:1080
# (NOTE: the compose stack's mailpit also binds 127.0.0.1:1025 — set OTP_SMTP_PORT
# or stop mailpit first; CI has no compose stack), 2. a second api (uvicorn, OTP
# mode) on :8100 — auth mode is picked at IMPORT time, so one process cannot serve
# both lanes. The api must trust the sink's self-signed cert BEFORE boot (#1146),
# hence one script. 3. a worker on its own Redis db index — it does the SMTP send
# (#1731). Optional env (DATABASE_URL, OTP_SMTP_PORT, OTP_REDIS_URL, ...) documented
# in frontend/e2e-otp/README.md.
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

OTP_API_PORT="${OTP_API_PORT:-8100}"
OTP_SMTP_PORT="${OTP_SMTP_PORT:-1025}"
OTP_SINK_PORT="${OTP_SINK_PORT:-1080}"
# An explicit template, and no `-t`.
OTP_STATE_DIR="${OTP_STATE_DIR:-$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dataq-otp-lane.XXXXXX")}"
mkdir -p "$OTP_STATE_DIR"

echo "otp lane state dir: $OTP_STATE_DIR"

# ── 1. SMTP sink ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python -m backend.scripts.e2e_otp_smtp_sink \
  --smtp-port "$OTP_SMTP_PORT" \
  --http-port "$OTP_SINK_PORT" \
  --cert-dir "$OTP_STATE_DIR" \
  >"$OTP_STATE_DIR/sink.log" 2>&1 &

> to only speak `ssl.create_default_context()` with no way to name a private CA,
> so DataQ couldn't talk to an internal relay on one without putting that CA in
> the process-wide trust store. `AUTH_EMAIL_CA_BUNDLE` (scoped to the mailer's own
> connection) and `AUTH_EMAIL_TLS_MODE=implicit` (SMTPS `:465`) now cover both gaps
> — see [#1146](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1146).

## Auth-mode injection

The mode is set per page as `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__` in `fixtures.ts` — which is
the **production contract**: nginx renders exactly that global from `DATAQ_AUTH_*`
env (ADR 0028), and `public/config.js` is an empty stub in dev, so nothing
clobbers it. No build-time flag, no test-only code path in `src/`.

```bash
# 1. Postgres + Redis reachable (docker compose up postgres redis), and a database to use.
createdb dataq_otp_e2e            # or reuse the e2e database

# 2. Backend half: SMTP sink + OTP-mode api + a worker. Blocks until all three are healthy.
DATABASE_URL=REDACTED \
  scripts/e2e-otp-stack.sh

27:export AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_PORT="$OTP_SMTP_PORT"

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.command:
N=$(gh issue create --title "a11y: the ratchet cannot detect under-reporting — a scan of a half-loaded page passes" --label enhancement --label test --label priority/P3 --milestone "v1.2 Backlog" --body "## Context
#1988 / PR #2050: the run-detail scan passed with 0 rows for weeks because it scanned before the results table loaded. The ratchet fails only on **new** rows, so *fewer* violations than the baseline is always green — it is structurally blind to a scan that saw less page than it should have.

\`settle()\` (PR #2050) removes the known cause (antd \`Spin\`/\`Skeleton\` still active, mount transitions in flight). Two gaps it does not cover, both verified **not reachable** by any currently-scanned route, recorded from the PR's review:

1. A loading state that is not a Spin/Skeleton — e.g. \`ComparisonCheckForm.tsx\`'s disabled-textarea \`Suspense\` fallback.
2. Two sequential spinners: \`toHaveCount(0)\` is 'eventually zero', not 'stays zero', so it can resolve in the gap.

## Suggested fix
Make under-reporting visible rather than chasing loading affordances one by one: in ratchet (non-capture) mode, report baseline rows for the scanned surface that were **not** observed — as a warning locally and a failure in CI unless the baseline is regenerated in the same PR. A surface whose violations all vanish without a code change is the exact signature #1988 had.

Refs #1670, #1980." | tail -1); echo $N

The fix was right for a reason I had not verified. Docstring corrected in ce07af09596d090028935c65f8d7c96d0c6c6418; PR body corrected.
- **Two latent gaps in \`settle\`** (non-Spin Suspense fallback; sequential spinners) — verified unreachable by every scanned route; filed with the underlying ratchet blind spot as $N.
- Baseline regen integrity verified: capture is a per-surface overwrite, and \`component:Results\` (5 rows) and \`route:/sign-in\` (1 row) are byte-identical before and after.

Not a bug.

  - **Tag CSS specificity / solid variant risk**: grepped `frontend/src` for `variant="solid"`, `variant='solid'`, `CheckableTag`, `bordered={false}` — zero matches. The new `.ant-tag.ant-tag-error` etc. rules only ever apply to the default pale-tint Tag backgrounds actually used in this codebase, so the solid/outlined-collision concern doesn't currently manifest as a live bug (worth a comment/guard if solid tags are added later, but not a current defect).

  ## Angle A — obvious/large bugs
  
  ### Issue 1 (real bug, high confidence): `Filter` silently fails to label its control when the caller renders a sibling node beside the control
  
  **File:** `frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminCompliance.tsx`, lines 118–131 (call site unchanged by this PR, but it consumes the `Filter` component this PR rewrote — `frontend/src/components/shared/Filter.tsx` lines 213–229).
  
  ```tsx
  <Filter label="Actor user ID">
    <Input ... />
    {actorError && (
      <Typography.Text type="danger" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>
        Not a valid ID — paste the UUID from the Members table, not an email.
      </Typography.Text>
    )}
  </Filter>
  ```
  
  `Filter`'s new implementation is:
  ```tsx
  const child = isValidElement(children) ? (children as ReactElement<{ id?: string }>) : null;
  const controlId = child?.props.id ?? generatedId;
  ...
  <label htmlFor={controlId}>...</label>
  {child ? cloneElement(child, { id: controlId }) : children}
  ```
  
  When a `Filter` call site has more than one JSX child (here: the `Input` plus the conditional `Typography.Text`), React always compiles this to an **array** of children — `[InputElement, (actorError && TextElement)]` — regardless of whether `actorError` is truthy or falsy at runtime (a falsy conditional still occupies a slot in the array, it doesn't vanish from the compiled arguments). `isValidElement(children)` therefore returns `false` unconditionally for this call site, `child` is always `null`, `controlId` falls back to the unused `generatedId`, and the raw `children` (the `Input` with no `id`) is rendered as-is. The `<label htmlFor={controlId}>` therefore points at an id that exists nowhere in the DOM — the exact "Form elements must have labels" violation this PR set out to fix, reintroduced at this one call site, always (not just when `actorError` is true).
  
  This is exactly the class of call site the review was asked to check for ("a wrapper... around the control"), and it's the one real instance found among the four files that call `<Filter>`. The other `Filter` call sites (`SamplePolicyPanel.tsx`, `DataSubjectCard.tsx`, `Results.tsx`) all pass a single child element and are unaffected.
  
  **Why CI didn't catch it:** `frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` (the Playwright axe lane referenced in the regenerated baseline) only scans `/admin` (the default Admin tab), not the `/admin` → Compliance sub-tab where `AdminCompliance` renders. `frontend/tests/a11y/components.a11y.test.tsx` (the Vitest axe lane) also does not include `AdminCompliance`/`SamplePolicyPanel`... actually `SamplePolicyPanel` isn't in that list either, but that one is unaffected since it has single children). So this regression is invisible to both automated a11y gates the PR relies on to justify zeroing the baseline.

|---|---|---|

(4) frontend/src/styles.css: light-theme tag text colours for green/orange/cyan/lime/yellow. (5) AdminIntegrations.tsx aria-labels. (6) new unit test tests/components/ScrollableTableFocus.test.tsx.

Does the dev-bypass API in CI return a plain list for these endpoints (check backend/app/api/v1 routers for pagination wrappers)? `assets[0]` — is the seeded asset list guaranteed non-empty and is ordering deterministic (see backend/scripts/seed_dev.py and the assets list service ORDER BY)? PR [#2055](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2055) is open and under review: the axe gate now covers **every route (9 → 21 surfaces)** with an empty baseline, and the 15 violations the new surfaces exposed are fixed.

The reviewer is pointed at the riskiest piece — the shell-level `ScrollableTableFocus` (whether it can clobber attributes rc-table sets itself, whether a body-wide `MutationObserver` reading `scrollWidth` thrashes layout on the 30s-polling and live-progress views, and whether a sider collapse leaves it stale without a `ResizeObserver`) — plus the blast radius of `colorTextTertiary`/`colorTextPlaceholder` and whether `assets[0]` is deterministic in CI. I'll act on what it finds, post the review and arm auto-merge, then start #1671.

**Track so far**

| | |
|---|---|
| Merged | #2050 (#1988 closed), #2052, #2053 (#1980 closed) |
| In review | #2055 (closes #2054) |
| Axe baseline | 107 → **0**, across 21 surfaces instead of 9 |
| Filed | #2048 dark-mode gate · #2049 page titles · #2051 ratchet blind spots · #2054 scan coverage |
| Queue | #1671 (P2) → #2048 → #1672 → #2049 → #1673 → #2051, then one `docs/progress.md` refresh and scratch-stack teardown |

  ## Finding 1 — Nested tables produce duplicate/nested identically-named "Scrollable table" landmarks (real, not hypothetical)
  
  **File:** `frontend/src/components/shared/ScrollableTableFocus.tsx` (all lines, esp. 109-119), interacting with `frontend/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx` (lines ~430-448 and ~568-580).
  
  RunDetail.tsx nests a *second* `<Table>` (the per-check "Failing rows" table, line 441, `scroll={{x:'max-content'}}`) inside `expandable.expandedRowRender` of the *outer* check-results table (line 569, also `scroll={{x:'max-content'}}`), which is not tab-hidden — both are simultaneously mounted and visible once a row with failing samples is expanded. If both overflow (routine: the outer results table has several columns, and failing-sample rows commonly have many/wide columns), `ScrollableTableFocus` marks BOTH `.ant-table-content` elements with `role="region" aria-label="Scrollable table"` at the same time — one physically nested inside the other, both with the identical accessible name. A screen-reader user navigating by landmarks gets two (or more, with multiple rows expanded) indistinguishable "Scrollable table" regions, one inside the other, with no way to tell which is which. I confirmed via `frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts`'s own new `route:/results/:id` scan doesn't necessarily exercise the expanded-row state, so this won't be caught by the ratchet, and axe's `region`/`landmark-unique` rules are `moderate` (not gated per CLAUDE.md's list), so CI stays green while the regression ships. Confirmed I checked Results.tsx's two `<Table>`s too — those are in an antd `Tabs` (line 103), so only one is ever un-hidden at a time and doesn't reproduce this; RunDetail.tsx's nested-table case does. Confidence: 80.
  
  ## Finding 2 — MutationObserver config can't see the exact changes this feature exists to react to
  
  **File:** `frontend/src/components/shared/ScrollableTableFocus.tsx`, lines 133-135 (`observer.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true })`).
  
  The observer is configured for `childList`/`subtree` only — it does not set `characterData: true`, so a pure text-node content change (no element added/removed) never fires it. React updates a cell whose *content* changes but whose element structure is unchanged via a `characterData` mutation on the text node, not a `childList` mutation. Results.tsx's pipeline-runs tab polls every 30s (`PIPELINE_POLL_MS`, line 373) and RunDetail has a live-progress view; a case where a cell's displayed text grows (e.g. a duration counter, a longer status string) without any row being added/removed would newly cause overflow with zero childList mutation anywhere in `document.body`, and zero `resize` event — so `sync()` never re-runs and the table stays non-focusable despite now overflowing (the exact failure mode the component exists to prevent). Conversely a table that stops overflowing this way keeps its stale `tabindex`/`role`. A CSS-only reflow (e.g. a flex/sider-driven width change with no element add/remove and no window resize) has the same gap; I verified the app's actual Sider-collapse path (`App.tsx` `onBreakpoint`→`setNarrow`) happens to also toggle child mounting (`{!narrow && <Menu/>}`, line 173) so it's incidentally covered by `childList`, but that's coincidental, not by design — a future narrow-viewport change that only changes CSS width would silently reintroduce the gap. Confidence: 60 (real, verified gap in the observer's reach; whether it fires in practice today depends on data shapes not fully enumerable from static review).
  
  ## Checked and found NOT to be bugs (ruled out with evidence)
  
  - **rc-table conflict:** Read `@rc-component/table@1.11.1`'s `Table.js` directly — `pickAttrs(props, ...)` (`ariaProps`) is spread onto the inner `<table>` element, never onto the `.ant-table-content`/`.ant-table-body` wrapper divs this component targets. No virtual/sticky tables are used anywhere in this app (`CheckEdit.tsx` explicitly sets `virtual={false}`; no `sticky` prop usage found). No clobbering.
  - **`colorLink: '#a5b4fc'` dark-mode seed re-transform (theme.ts:210):** Traced the actual antd v6 pipeline (`genColorMapToken.js` + `generate()` from `@ant-design/colors`) and computed real output values. The applied `colorLink` becomes `#8f9cd9` (a palette-derived shade, not the literal `#a5b4fc`) — but I computed its contrast against `--dq-surface` (`#161b22`) at **6.53:1**, comfortably clearing AA (and clearing the comment's claimed old `4.36:1`/`4.50:1` problem value). The PR's inline comment describes the *old* problem value accurately and never claims `#a5b4fc` renders verbatim, so there's no false claim either. Not a bug — the seed-retransform mechanic is real but the fix still achieves its goal. (`colorLinkHover`/`colorLinkActive` land below AA at 2.64:1/4.27:1, but this is pre-existing behavior — the old code had the same shape at 2.07:1/3.10:1 — and this PR's change makes both *less* bad, not worse, so it's not a regression this PR introduces.)
  - **`colorTextTertiary`/`colorTextPlaceholder` (theme.ts:75,77):** Confirmed via `alias.js`/`genColorMapToken.js` that `colorTextDisabled` derives from `colorTextQuaternary` (unchanged, still ~0.25 alpha), not from `colorTextPlaceholder`, so no component conflates disabled text with placeholder text. `colorTextTertiary` (now 0.6) feeds `colorIcon` (table sorter/filter icons, tag close icons, tabs, etc.) and is close to but distinct from `colorTextSecondary` (unchanged default 0.65) — a minor hierarchy compression, not a functional break; treating as a nitpick per instructions.
  - **e2e spec (`request` in `beforeAll`, proxy resolution, endpoint shapes):** `playwright.config.ts`'s `use.baseURL` applies to the `request` fixture in `beforeAll` (standard, documented Playwright behavior); `vite.config.ts` proxies `/api` to the backend. `GET /suites` and `GET /assets` both use `response_model=list[...]` (plain arrays, no pagination envelope), matching the spec's `.json()` usage. `seed_dev.py` → `seed_demo_data()` (`backend/scripts/demo_data.py`) unconditionally creates the "Orders quality" suite with checks and an asset target, so the seeded-data assumptions hold.
  - **`getByText('404')` strict-mode risk:** `ErrorState.tsx`'s 404 catalog entry renders `<Result status="404" title="404 — Not found">`; antd's `PRESENTED_IMAGE_404` SVG (`noFound.js`) contains no literal "404" text nodes (grepped source), so there's exactly one text match. Admin sub-page heading assertions are all backed by one shared `AdminLayout.tsx` `<Typography.Title level={3}>Admin</Typography.Title>`, consistent across all six sub-routes.
  - **CONTRIBUTING rule 15c (no ticket numbers in UI text):** All new UI-facing strings (`aria-label="Scrollable table"`, the two AdminIntegrations aria-labels) are ticket-number-free; issue/PR references appear only in code comments, which the rule doesn't cover.
  - **Rule 4b baseline:** New route scans use the existing ratchet mechanism (`frontend/scripts/a11y/ratchet.ts`), which only fails on violations not already recorded for a given surface key — consistent with how every prior route in this spec already works; no baseline-file changes were needed for this to be correct.
  
  No other obvious large bugs found in the diff.
</agent-message>

Part 1 of #1671 (non-colour severity cues): tags and score readouts. Charts and the colourblind-safe palette are part 2.

- **The `Checks n/m` chip was the one genuinely colour-only severity encoding in the tables.** It shows a ratio; the run's worst severity existed only as the chip's colour — `1/2` in magenta vs `2/4` in red was the entire difference between *critical* and *fail*. It now carries that severity's glyph and an accessible name (`1 of 2 checks passed, worst result critical`).
- New shared `ResultStatusTag` / `RunStatusTag` / `ChecksOutcomeTag` (`components/shared/StatusTag.tsx`): every status has its **own** glyph (pass ✓, warn ⚠, fail ✕, critical flame, skip −, error !; queued clock, running spinner, cancelled stop). Replaces the hand-rolled `<Tag color={…_COLORS[s]}>` at the run/result call sites in Results, RunDetail, RecentRuns, LiveRunProgress and DryRunPreview.
- Suite Performance's state label and the asset scorecard's readout used the **fill** scale as text: "Optimal" rendered `#52c41a` on white, 2.2:1, and antd paints a 100% `Progress` readout the same green. New `SEVERITY_TEXT` tokens (`--dq-severity-*-text`, per theme) for text; the fill scale is unchanged for bars. axe does not evaluate that label at all (placed in none of its result buckets — recorded on #2051), so the empty baseline never covered it.

Refs #1671

- [x] feat — new functionality

- [x] **Manually tested locally**

- [x] No schema change

## Security / risk notes

Visual: every run/result tag gains a leading icon, so those columns are ~18px wider. Not yet migrated, deliberately — they are string-typed rather than `ResultStatus`/`RunStatus` and need their own mapping: pipeline-run status (`pipelineStatusColor`), incident status/severity, asset health, `CheckTrend`'s table. Tracked for part 2 with the charts.

Code review of GitHub PR #2056 in repo TheurgicDuke771/DataQ (working dir /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; the PR branch is checked out, so files on disk are the PR head). READ-ONLY: do NOT run git checkout/switch/stash/reset or modify any file. Use `gh pr diff 2056`. Do not build, typecheck or run tests.

PR summary (accessibility, WCAG 1.4.1 use-of-colour): NEW frontend/src/components/shared/StatusTag.tsx exporting `ResultStatusTag`, `RunStatusTag`, `ChecksOutcomeTag` — antd `Tag` with a per-status `icon` and, for the checks chip, an `aria-label` like "1 of 2 checks passed, worst result critical". Call sites in pages/Results.tsx, pages/RunDetail.tsx, components/dashboard/RecentRuns.tsx, components/runs/LiveRunProgress.tsx, components/checks/DryRunPreview.tsx were switched from `<Tag color={RESULT_STATUS_COLORS[s]}>{s}</Tag>`. Also: `SEVERITY_TEXT` tokens in theme.ts + `--dq-severity-*-text` CSS vars per theme in styles.css, used for SuitePerformance's state label; `Progress` `format` now returns a span with `color: var(--dq-ink)` in SuitePerformance and ScorecardPanel. New test tests/components/StatusTag.test.tsx.

Scan for OBVIOUS, LARGE bugs in changed lines, verifying against the real code:
 1. content.text:
PR [#2056](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2056) (part 1 of #1671) is open and under review. I've pointed the reviewer at the thing I'm least sure of: `aria-label` on a role-less `<span>` is prohibited by ARIA 1.2 (`role=generic`), so the checks chip's accessible name may not actually be announced — and the antd icons may be announcing themselves as "fire 1/2". If either holds, the fix is a visually-hidden text node and `aria-hidden` glyphs; I'll make that change when the review lands.

**Session summary**

| PR | Issue | State |
|---|---|---|
| #2050 | #1988 scan determinism | **Merged**, closed |
| #2052 | #1980 contrast tokens | **Merged** |
| #2053 | #1980 labels + Progress names | **Merged**, #1980 closed |
| #2055 | #2054 every route scanned (9 → 21 surfaces) | Reviewed, auto-merge armed |
| #2056 | #1671 part 1 — non-colour status cues | In review |

Axe baseline: **107 → 0**, now across every route in both the ratchet and a manual dark-mode pass.

**Filed:** #2048 (dark mode ungated) · #2049 (static page titles) · #2051 (ratchet blind spots — now three recorded: under-reporting, overlays never opened, and a low-contrast node axe silently doesn't evaluate) · #2054.

**Remaining, in order:** #1671 part 2 (red/green chart, marker shapes, string-typed tags, reduced motion) → #2048 → #1672 keyboard → #2049 titles → #1673 screen-reader semantics → #2051. Then one `docs/progress.md` Snapshot refresh and teardown of the two scratch stacks (`dataq_a11y`, `dataq_otp_a11y`, the `a11y-scratch` OpenBao mount).

Every review this session caught something the automated gate couldn't — a wrong root cause, a Tooltip regression to 1.88:1, a dangling label on an unscanned tab, landmark flooding and a blind `MutationObserver`. That's the argument for keeping `/code-review` on every one of these, small as they look.

  - **Dark/light `--dq-severity-*-text` contrast:** recomputed WCAG contrast ratios programmatically — light (`#237804`/`#874d00`/`#cf1322`/`#595959` on `#ffffff`): 5.59/6.79/5.57/7.00:1; dark (`#73d13d`/`#ffc53d`/`#ff7875`/`#bfbfbf` on `#161b22`): 8.99/10.96/6.75/9.41:1. No behavioural regressions at the swapped call sites, no broken tests, contrast is fine.

---
name: feedback-axe-gate-blind-spots
description: A green axe scan / empty a11y baseline proves little — six concrete ways it lied in one session, and the ARIA/antd traps behind them
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

An empty axe baseline means "no serious violation in what was rendered, on the surfaces visited, that axe chose to evaluate." In one session (2026-09-21) it was wrong six ways:

1. **Scanned before the content loaded** (#1988): the route landmark was visible while the table sat behind its `loading` Spin, so the 13 failing nodes weren't in the DOM. The ratchet only fails on NEW rows, so *fewer* violations is always green. My first explanation (axe "incomplete" under a 0.5 blur) was wrong — a reviewer's note that no `<Spin spinning>` wrapper existed made me probe and disprove it. Same lesson as [[feedback-verify-the-reason-not-just-the-result]].
2. **Overlays never open**: a global dark `colorTextLightSolid` took Tooltip text to 1.88:1 across 22 files; nothing in the spec hovers anything. antd global tokens have huge blast radius — scope to `components.Button`/`components.Avatar`.
3. **Unscanned surfaces**: 9 of 21 routes were scanned; the rest held 13 serious violations.
4. **Dark mode** unscanned (#2048) — it had its own failures.
5. **A node axe silently skips**: inline-coloured `<strong>` severity text at 2.2:1 appeared in none of passes/violations/incomplete/inapplicable.
6. **Things axe can't judge at all**: `aria-label` on a role-less `<span>` (antd `Tag`) is dropped — ARIA makes `role=generic` name-prohibited; use visually-hidden text. `@ant-design/icons` render `role="img" aria-label="<icon-name>"`, so a decorative glyph announces "fire 1/2" — add `aria-hidden`. `role="region"` per table floods landmarks (use `group`).

**Why:** each of these shipped green and was caught only by `/code-review` agents reading antd/rc-table source or by a hand probe.

**How to apply:** for any a11y change, verify in Chromium's **accessibility tree** (`locator.ariaSnapshot()`), not the DOM and never jsdom; probe dark mode and at least one open overlay by hand; mutation-check that an empty baseline can FAIL (remove the fix, expect `[NEW]`); when a `MutationObserver` watches for layout effects, pair it with a `ResizeObserver` — `childList` cannot see text growing or a CSS reflow. `Filter`-style wrappers that `cloneElement` must handle array children (`{cond && <Hint/>}` makes children an array even when falsy).

## Summary

Part 2a of #1671: the charts.

- **Quality Trends** stacked failed-red on succeeded-green with two identical round legend dots — the pair most colour-vision deficiencies merge. The failed series is now **diagonally hatched** (an SVG `<pattern>`), so the two read apart in greyscale; the legend swatch inherits the hatch from the bar's own fill, so the key always matches the mark. Legend labels were also painted in the series colour ("Succeeded" `#52c41a` = 2.2:1, "Failed" 3.3:1) — now ink.
- **Check trend** points encoded status by dot colour alone. New `charts/StatusMarker`: pass dot · warn triangle · fail square · critical diamond · skip hollow ring · error cross. The passing majority stays a quiet dot; every non-pass outcome gets its own silhouette.

## Linked issue

Refs #1671

- [x] feat — new functionality

- [x] **Manually tested locally**

- [x] **Security implications considered** — none

## Schema migration?

- [x] No schema change

- Quality Trends screenshotted in Chromium, light and dark: hatch visible in the bar and the legend swatch in both; legend text ink in both.

Remaining under #1671: a colourblind-safe **fill** palette (`--dq-severity-*` — graphics need 3:1 against the surface, WCAG 1.4.11; gold `#faad14` and grey `#bfbfbf` do not reach it on white), a shape key beside the check-trend chart, and the string-typed tags (pipeline status, incidents, asset health) — the last waits on #2056's `StatusTag`.

A watcher is waiting on #2055 to merge and will then report whether #2056 went CONFLICTING (both touch `styles.css` / `theme.ts`); I'll merge main into it if so. After #2057's review: the fill palette + string-typed tags to finish #1671, then #2048 → #1672 → #2049 → #1673 → #2051, a single `docs/progress.md` refresh, and scratch-stack teardown.

**What the six reviews caught that the gate could not** — each would have shipped green:
1. My root cause for #1988 was wrong (rows weren't loaded; nothing to do with axe's "incomplete").
2. A global dark token took Tooltip text to 1.88:1 in 22 files.
3. A label dangling on an unscanned admin tab — which led to #2054 and 13 more violations.

cat > $S/pr8.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

Closes out #1671.

- **Severity fills reach 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11, graphical marks).** On the light theme the bars were antd's -6 shades: green 2.27, gold 1.90, grey 1.84 on white — and red, 3.27 on white, drops under 3 on the `#f4f5f7` canvas. Light now uses `#389e0d` / `#c77d05` / `#f5222d` / `#8c8c8c` (+ `--dq-error` `#d4380d`); dark keeps the brighter shades, which already clear 3:1 on the dark surface, by redeclaring them in the dark block.
- **`tests/a11y/tokens.test.ts`** parses `styles.css` and holds the token *values* to the ratios in both themes against both backgrounds: fills + critical/error ≥ 3:1, the `-text` tokens + `--dq-muted` ≥ 4.5:1. This is the guard #2051 asked for — axe cannot see an SVG fill or a `<Progress>` stroke, and silently skips some inline-coloured text.
- **A shape key under the check-trend chart** (`StatusMarkerKey`), listing only the statuses actually plotted, in severity order. #2057 added the shapes; without a key they were a code nobody was given.
- **The remaining status tags move to the shared component**: incident evidence (×3), incident severity, the check-trend table, pipeline-run status. `ResultStatusTag` / `RunStatusTag` now accept the plain `string` those API shapes carry, rendering an unknown value as a neutral glyph-less tag. `pipelineStatusColor` (and an orphaned, mid-sentence comment fragment above it) is deleted as dead; its "unknown status" guarantee moves to a test on the shared tag.

Deliberately not changed: incident *lifecycle* status (`open` / `acknowledged`) and `AssetHealthTag` — both already render a word, so neither was colour-only, and neither maps onto the result/run vocabularies.

## Linked issue

Fixes #1671

- [x] feat — new functionality

## Checklist

- [x] **Manually tested locally**
- [x] **Single functionality**
- [x] **Conventional commit title**
- [x] **No secrets, credentials, or `.env` files committed**
- [x] **Prettier + ESLint pass locally**
- [x] **Tests added/updated**
- [ ] **`/code-review` agent review run on this PR**
- [x] **`docs/progress.md` — N/A** for this PR
- [x] **Security implications considered** — none

## Schema migration?

- [x] No schema change

## Manual test notes

- Token test: 22/22 on the new values; run against the previous `styles.css` it fails on exactly the four old fills (incl. red, which passes on white and fails on the canvas).
- Dashboard reviewed in Chromium: deeper green/red bars, hatch intact, Suite Performance strokes legible against the track.
- Unit suite 129 files / 1415 tests. E2E: a11y (all surfaces) + results + assets + dashboard + check-editor green.
- **Still not verified in-app:** the shape key and markers on a live check-trend chart — no seeded check has plotted trend history. Covered by unit tests only.

## Security / risk notes

Visual: every severity bar, dot and `Progress` stroke on the light theme is a deeper shade.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Code review of GitHub PR #2060 in repo TheurgicDuke771/DataQ (working dir /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; the PR branch is checked out, so files on disk are the PR head). READ-ONLY: do NOT run git checkout/switch/stash/reset or modify any file. Use `gh pr diff 2060`. Do not build, typecheck or run tests.

PR summary (accessibility): (1) frontend/src/styles.css — light-theme `--dq-severity-{good,warning,bad,neutral}` and `--dq-error` changed to darker 3:1 fills; the dark block now REDECLARES the old brighter values. (2) NEW frontend/tests/a11y/tokens.test.ts parses styles.css with a regex and asserts WCAG ratios per theme. (3) frontend/src/components/charts/StatusMarker.tsx gains `StatusMarkerKey`, mounted under the metric chart in components/checks/CheckTrend.tsx. (4) components/shared/StatusTag.tsx: `ResultStatusTag`/`RunStatusTag` accept `string`, unknown → neutral glyph-less tag; call sites swapped in IncidentEvidenceDrawer, IncidentsPanel, CheckTrend table, and the pipeline-runs table in pages/Results.tsx. (5) `pipelineStatusColor` deleted from components/results/resultsFormat.ts with its test.

Scan for OBVIOUS, LARGE bugs in the changed lines, verifying against real code:
 1. PIPELINE STATUS REGRESSION (most important): the old `pipelineStatusColor(status)` mapped provider-agnostic pipeline statuses. The new code renders `<RunStatusTag status={s} />`, keyed by the DQ RunStatus vocabulary (queued|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled). What values can `pipeline_runs.status` actually take? Check backend (backend/app/db/models.py PipelineRun + any CHECK constraint / PIPELINE_RUN_STATUSES, backend/app/orchestration/*, the ADF/Airflow/dbt status normalisation) and the frontend type in frontend/src/api/runs.ts or orchestration.ts. If pipeline statuses include values NOT in RunStatus (e.g. 'in_progress', 'skipped', 'unknown', 'upstream_failed'), those previously got 'default' colour and still do — fine — but confirm no pipeline status that USED to get a colour now loses it, and no DQ-run-only glyph is misapplied.
 2. The dark block redeclaration: does `:root[data-theme='dark']` fully restore every token the light block changed (good/warning/bad/neutral/error), so dark mode is visually unchanged? Is `--dq-critical` consistent? Any OTHER place that depended on the light values being antd's exact -6 shades — e.g. frontend/src/auth/LoginPage.tsx uses RESULT_STATUS_CHART_COLORS on a hard-coded WHITE card regardless of theme: in DARK mode that card is still white but now gets the dark block's BRIGHT fills (unchanged from before, so not a regression — confirm), and any `@media print` rules in styles.css (the PDF export prints on white: does print force light tokens or would a dark-theme user's print get bright-on-white fills — pre-existing or changed?).
 3. tokens.test.ts: the `block()` regex helper — `css.indexOf(':root {')` finds the FIRST `:root {`; is that the light token block, or could an earlier `:root` rule / comment containing that text match first? It slices to the first `\n}` — are there nested braces (e.g. @media inside) that would truncate the block early and silently drop tokens, making `vars[token]` undefined → `luminance(undefined)` throws (loud, fine) or passes vacuously? Does the 6-hex-digit regex silently skip tokens declared as rgba()/3-digit hex so a future non-hex token is never checked? Is `__dirname` defined under this repo's vitest/ESM config (check other tests for the pattern they use, e.g. `import.meta.url`)?
 4. `StatusMarkerKey` in CheckTrend: `withMetric.map((p) => p.status as ResultStatus)` — with a status outside the union the key filters by KEY_ORDER so it is simply omitted while the chart shows a hollow ring for it: acceptable? Any layout issue mounting a `<ul>` there (is the parent a Flex/Card that expects specific children)?
 5. Deleted `pipelineStatusColor`: any remaining importer anywhere (src, tests, e2e, docs code samples)?
 6. CLAUDE.md / CONTRIBUTING.md rules that SPECIFICALLY apply.

Ignore nitpicks, linter/typechecker-catchable items, pre-existing issues on untouched lines. For each issue: file + line range, what breaks, evidence, confidence 0-100. If none, say "no issues".

content.text:
PR [#2060](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2060) is open — it closes out #1671 — and under review. The reviewer's main target is the swap I'm least sure of: pipeline-run status now renders through `RunStatusTag`, which is keyed by the DQ-run vocabulary, so I've asked it to trace what values `pipeline_runs.status` can actually hold in the backend and confirm nothing that used to get a colour loses it. It's also checking that the new token test's CSS parsing can't pass vacuously.

**Where things stand**

| PR | Issue | State |
|---|---|---|
| #2050, #2052, #2053, #2055, #2056, #2057 | #1988, #1980, #2054 closed | **Merged**; `main` verified green with all six combined |
| #2058 | `docs/progress.md` Snapshot refresh | Reviewed, armed |
| #2059 | the one route the gate missed (`/connections/:id/edit`) → 22 surfaces | Armed |
| #2060 | #1671 — 3:1 fills, token-contrast test, shape key, remaining tags | In review |

New in #2060 and worth calling out: `tests/a11y/tokens.test.ts` holds the severity/muted token *values* to WCAG ratios in both themes. It's the first guard in the repo for things axe structurally can't see (SVG fills, `Progress` strokes, the inline-coloured text it silently skips), and it fails on exactly the four old fills.

**After #2060:** #2048 (dark-mode gate — dark is already clean, so an empty baseline from day one) → #1672 keyboard → #2049 titles → #1673 screen-reader semantics → #2051, then scratch-stack teardown. Nothing from this track is deployed yet; it's all frontend, no migrations.

One dead CSS rule (`:root[data-theme='dark'] .ant-tag.ant-tag-error`) is removed from frontend/src/styles.css. frontend/e2e/README.md's a11y section is rewritten.

Does the provider resolve the mode synchronously enough that `data-theme` is set before the scan, or could the `toHaveAttribute` assertion flake on first paint (it auto-retries — fine)? Is there a server-side/user-profile theme preference that could override localStorage in the dev-bypass lane?

Check playwright.config.ts for fullyParallel/workers and reason about it concretely.

The outer describe title now includes `[light]`/`[dark]` — confirm every test's full title path is unique (including the looped `admin ${sub}` tests and the id-addressed loop), otherwise Playwright errors at collection time.

'#ff7875' : …`) and that no OTHER consumer relied on that CSS rule (e.g. a tag rendered OUTSIDE antd's ConfigProvider — the login page? — where the token would not apply but the global CSS rule did). grep for `color="error"` Tag usages in frontend/src/auth.

## Summary

 8. CLAUDE.md / CONTRIBUTING.md rules that SPECIFICALLY apply (e.g. rule 15c UI text; hard-coded user-facing strings).

Ignore nitpicks, linter/typechecker-catchable items, pre-existing issues on untouched lines EXCEPT item 5, where remaining mouse-only navigations are wanted explicitly. For each issue: file + line range, what breaks, evidence, confidence 0-100.

content.text:
PR [#2063](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2063) — first slice of #1672 (keyboard) — is open and under review.

**What it fixes:** runs and assets couldn't be opened without a mouse (rows navigated via `onClick` with no link in any cell); there was no skip link; and client-side navigation left focus on a link that often no longer existed. Verified in Chromium with a new `e2e/keyboard.spec.ts` — which promptly caught a bug in my own first attempt (React StrictMode double-running the effect put focus on `<main>` at load, so the first Tab skipped the skip link).

**What I've asked the reviewer to attack:** the focus-on-navigation effect fires on *every* pathname change, and I suspect it's too blunt. Two flows worry me — the Admin sub-pages are tab-like (clicking a tab would yank focus off the tab bar), and Suites is master/detail at `/suites/:id` (selecting a suite would throw a keyboard user out of the list each time). If the reviewer confirms either, the fix is to scope the focus move to top-level section changes. I've also asked for an inventory of every remaining mouse-only navigation in `src/`.

**Track status**

| | |
|---|---|
| Merged (9) | #2050, #2052, #2053, #2055, #2056, #2057, #2058, #2059, #2060 |
| Armed | #2062 — dark-mode gate (closes #2048) |
| In review | #2063 — keyboard, slice 1 (#1672) |
| Issues closed | #1988, #1980, #2054, #1671 |
| Filed | #2048, #2049, #2051, #2054, #2061 |

Remaining after these: rest of #1672 (Monaco Tab trap, lineage graph, drawer/modal focus audit) → #2049 → #1673 → #2051 → #2061, then scratch-stack teardown. Nothing from the track is deployed; it's all frontend with no migrations.
