  Reviewed PR #2063 against the actual code on the PR head (not just the diff). Findings below, grouped by the numbered items in the brief; each has file:line, what breaks/doesn't, evidence, and confidence.
  
  ## 1. Focus-on-navigation blast radius
  
  **(a) Admin tabs — REAL, but narrower than the hypothesis. Confidence 65.**
  `frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:19-38` — `<Tabs activeKey={active} onChange={(key) => navigate(`/admin/${key}`)} .../>`. Checked `@rc-component/tabs` (`node_modules/.../@rc-component/tabs/es/TabNavList/index.js:289-367`): this is the **manual-activation** WAI-ARIA pattern — `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` only call `onOffset` to move visual DOM focus between tab buttons; only `Enter`/`Space` (or a click) call `onTabClick`, which is what fires `onChange`. So arrow-key traversal of the tab bar itself is *not* broken by the new effect. But every tab **activation** (click, or Enter after arrowing) calls `navigate()`, which changes `location.pathname`, which fires `App.tsx`'s new effect (`App.tsx:97-101`) and calls `mainRef.current?.focus()` — yanking DOM focus from the tab button to `<main>`. A keyboard user who activates a tab and wants to check the next one must Tab all the way back to the tab list instead of picking up where they left off. Real regression, just not the literal "breaks arrow-key traversal" framing.
  
  **(b) Suites master/detail — NOT a bug as hypothesized; reveals a separate pre-existing gap. Confidence 85.**
  `frontend/src/pages/Suites.tsx:195` (`onSelect={(id) => navigate(...)}`) and `:267-289` (`SimpleList.Item onClick`, `.dq-suite-row`). Checked `frontend/src/components/SimpleList.tsx:70-117` — `SimpleListItem` is a plain `<div onClick>` with **no `tabIndex`, no `onKeyDown`, no `role="button"`** (confirmed: zero matches for `tabIndex|onKeyDown` in either file). So the row is not keyboard-focusable *at all* today — a keyboard user can't "arrow/tab through suites" to begin with, so there's no keyboard focus for the new effect to steal. For a mouse click it's harmless (nothing was keyboard-focused). This reframes into the item-5 finding below: `.dq-suite-row` is a genuine mouse-only nav element, and `styles.css:108` already has a `.dq-suite-row:focus-visible` rule that can never fire, i.e. someone expected this to be keyboard-operable and it isn't.
  
  **(c) Steppers — verified benign.** `ConnectionNew.tsx:22` picks the connection type via local `useState`, not a route change (`/connections/new` stays the same URL), so no mid-form focus theft. No other pathname-changing wizard found.
  
  **(d) Route-driven drawers/modals — N/A.** `CheckNew`/`CheckEdit`/`SuiteEdit`/`ConnectionEdit` are all full lazy-loaded page routes, not overlay drawers mounted on a route transition. None found.
  
  **(e) Scroll container — informational, not a regression from this PR. Confidence 55.** Grepped all of `frontend/src` for `ScrollToTop|scrollTo|scrollIntoView|preventScroll`: zero matches. There is no scroll-restoration on navigation today, pre-existing and untouched by this PR — `Content`'s `scrollTop` carries over across routes (e.g. landing mid-scroll on `/results/:id` after clicking a link from partway down a long list). `mainRef.current.focus()` with no `{preventScroll:true}` could itself trigger a scroll-into-view, but since `<main>` already fills the viewport this is unlikely to move anything. Worth a follow-up issue, but out of this PR's diff.
  
  ## 2. antd Content ref — verified benign, no bug.
  `node_modules/antd/es/layout/layout.js`: `Content = generator({suffixCls:'content', tagName:'main'})(Basic)`; both `generator`'s `Adapter` and `Basic` are `React.forwardRef` and pass `ref` straight to the `<TagName>` (`<main>`) DOM node. `ref={mainRef}` on `<Content>` correctly lands on the real `<main>` element; `useRef<HTMLElement>` is type-compatible; `page.locator('main#dq-main')` in the e2e spec is correct.
  
  ## 3. Skip link clipping — verified benign (reasoned from source, not browser-rendered). Confidence 75.
  `Layout` itself is `position: static` (confirmed via `layout.js` / `style/index.js` — only flex/background props, no `position`), and none of `html`/`body`/`#root` set `position` either (`styles.css:76-97`). Because the immediate DOM parent of `.dq-skip-link` is non-positioned, it does **not** establish a containing block for the `position:absolute` skip link — this is the standard "absolute descendant escapes a non-positioned ancestor's `overflow:hidden`" behavior, so the Layout's `overflow:hidden` does not clip it. Its `z-index:1100` also wins against `Header` (which is `position:static` and therefore always paints below any positioned element, regardless of DOM order or z-index value), so on focus it renders above the header rather than behind it. The e2e `toBeInViewport()` check happens to be sufficient here because nothing else is positioned at that layer to occlude it — but this was luck-of-the-layout rather than something the test itself proves.
  
  ## 4. RowLink inside ellipsis Text — real, concrete finding. Confidence 65.
  `frontend/src/pages/Assets.tsx:177-182` — `RowLink` is nested inside `<Typography.Text strong ellipsis style={{display:'block'}}>`, which antd renders with `overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap` on itself. An ancestor `overflow:hidden` clips descendant paint at its own box edge, including the `outline` drawn by the global `a:focus-visible {outline: 2px solid ...; outline-offset: 2px}` rule (`styles.css:106-111`) — so the focus ring on a truncated asset-name link will be asymmetrically clipped (visible on the left, cut off on the right, exactly where the name is long enough to ellipsis). This is a WCAG 2.4.7-relevant regression specific to Assets; the Results/RecentRuns `RowLink` usages are **not** wrapped in an `ellipsis` Text, so they don't have this problem.
  
  ## 5. Remaining mouse-only navigation (explicitly in scope even though pre-existing)
  - `frontend/src/pages/Suites.tsx:267-289` — the suite master-list row (`SimpleList.Item`/`.dq-suite-row`, `onClick={() => onSelect(suite.id)}`). Confirmed no `tabIndex`/`role="button"`/`onKeyDown` anywhere in `Suites.tsx` or `SimpleList.tsx`. `styles.css:108` already carries a dead `.dq-suite-row:focus-visible` rule that nothing can ever trigger. Confidence 90.
  - `frontend/src/pages/Suites.tsx:338-353` — `SuiteBrowseCard` (`<Card className="dq-card--interactive" onClick={onSelect}>`, the suite grid view). Same gap; `.dq-card--interactive:focus-visible` (`styles.css:107`) is equally unreachable. Confidence 90.
  - `frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx:470-493` — the Pipeline Runs tab's "DQ run" column: `<Tag style={{cursor:'pointer'}} onClick={() => navigate(`/results/${r.id}`)}>{r.status}</Tag>` per triggered run. A `Tag` (span) with a raw `onClick`, no keyboard affordance at all — a second, uncovered mouse-only path into a run's detail page from the same page this PR otherwise fixed. Confidence 90.
  - Checked `PipelineRunsTab`'s own `<Table>` (`Results.tsx:548`) — it has no `onRow`, so there's no missed row-level nav there, only the Tag above.
  
  ## 6. Existing unit tests — sanity-checked, fine.
  `frontend/tests/pages/Results.test.tsx`, `Dashboard.test.tsx`, `Assets.test.tsx` are all wrapped in `MemoryRouter` (grepped and confirmed), so `RowLink` (which needs Router context) renders without error in all three.
  
  ## 7. e2e/keyboard.spec.ts
  - `getByText('All assets')` (`keyboard.spec.ts:50`): Playwright's `getByText` substring-matches by default. `Assets.tsx` has the string "All assets" in two places — the `Segmented` option label (`Assets.tsx:58`) and the tree-view truncation `Alert`'s description ("...switch to \"All assets\" to page through the rest.", `Assets.tsx:146`). The alert only renders `if (items.length < total)` under the 2000-row tree-walk cap, so it won't be present under normal/seed data — the locator is effectively unique today but is a latent double-match hazard if a test environment's asset count ever exceeds the cap. Confidence 40 (latent, not currently broken).
  - Order-independence: each test gets its own fresh `page` fixture by default and all four specs are read-only navigations; no shared-state hazard found. Confidence 60 (no deep risk, not exhaustively proven).
  - Test `'clicking a row still opens the run, once — Back returns to the list'` (`keyboard.spec.ts:40-46`) only clicks `a.dq-row-link` itself — nothing in the suite clicks elsewhere in the row (e.g. the Status cell) to prove `onRow`'s own `onClick` still fires exactly once for a non-link click, which is exactly the interaction `RowLink`'s `stopPropagation()` is designed to coexist with. A regression to the row-level click path wouldn't be caught. Confidence 70.
  
  ## 8. CLAUDE.md / CONTRIBUTING rules
  Checked rule 15c (`scripts/check-frontend-no-ticket-refs.py`, frontend UI text must never cite an ADR/issue/PR number). Only new user-facing string is "Skip to content"; every `#nnnn` reference in the diff sits inside a `{/* JSX comment */}` or `//` comment, which the hook exempts. No violation.
  
  ## Not flagged / verified benign
  - `RowLink`'s `e.stopPropagation()` vs react-router `Link`'s own click handling: traced the composition — `Link`'s internal navigation runs in the same synchronous handler chain as the passed `onClick`, so `stopPropagation()` correctly prevents the event from also reaching the antd row's `onRow.onClick` via bubbling, without needing `preventDefault()`. No double-navigation.
  
</agent-message>

content.text:
#2062 merged (**#2048 closed**). #2063 is reviewed, re-verified on the combined state (44 a11y scans + 8 keyboard tests green after merging `main`), armed, and CI is running; a watcher will report when it lands.

**Accessibility track — end of day, 2026-09-21**

| | |
|---|---|
| Merged (10) | #2050, #2052, #2053, #2055, #2056, #2057, #2058, #2059, #2060, #2062 |
| Armed | #2063 — keyboard slice 1 (#1672) |
| Issues closed | #1988, #1980, #2054, #1671, #2048 |
| Filed, open | #2049 titles · #2051 gate blind spots · #2061 print from dark · #2064 scroll on navigation |

**What changed for users** (all frontend, no migrations, **nothing deployed yet**):
- Text, tags, bars and links meet contrast in both themes; status is carried by glyph/shape/hatch, not just colour.
- Every filter and progress bar has a real accessible name; overflowing tables scroll from the keyboard.
- Runs, assets and suites open without a mouse; there's a skip link; focus follows navigation.

**What changed for the team:** the axe gate went from 9 light-only surfaces with 107 baselined violations to **every route × both themes (44 scans), baseline 0**, plus a token-contrast test for values axe can't see and a real-browser keyboard spec. CONTRIBUTING rule 4b and the E2E README now describe that gate accurately.

**Three caveats I'd want you to have**
1. **The gate is a floor.** Nine of ten reviews found a real defect it structurally couldn't — that's the case for keeping `/code-review` on even tiny a11y PRs.
2. **Two tests don't prove what they look like they prove**, and the PRs say so: the admin-tab focus test passes with its fix removed (rc-tabs re-takes focus itself), and the trend markers / shape key have never been seen on a live chart because no seeded check has trend history.
3. I pushed once before running the repo-wide `format:check`; caught and fixed within minutes, but it's the rule you've already given me.

**Next:** rest of #1672 (Monaco Tab trap, lineage graph, drawer/modal focus audit) → #2049 → #1673 → #2051 → #2061 → #2064, then a `docs/progress.md` refresh for the post-#2058 PRs and teardown of the scratch stacks (DBs `dataq_a11y` / `dataq_otp_a11y`, the `a11y-scratch` OpenBao mount, processes on :8001 / :3001 / :8100). Track state and lessons are saved to memory for the next session.

cat > $S/pr12.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

- Every route shared the one static `<title>DataQ</title>` (WCAG 2.4.2). A screen reader announced nothing about where a navigation landed, and browser history / the tab strip showed N identical entries. `document.title` is now set from the path on every navigation: `Results · DataQ`, `Members · Admin · DataQ`, `Edit check · DataQ`, `Not found · DataQ`.
- One pure function, `utils/pageTitle.ts`, rather than a hook call in each of ~20 pages — a page that is never visited in a test cannot forget to title itself, and the mapping is unit-testable against the route list.
- `RunDetail` already set a richer title once its run loads (the suite name; it doubles as the Save-as-PDF filename, #345). That still wins — it is set later and restores the path title on unmount.

## Linked issue

Fixes #2049

## Type of change

- [x] fix — bug fix (linked issue above)

## Checklist

- [x] **Manually tested locally**
- [x] **Single functionality**
- [x] **Conventional commit title**
- [x] **No secrets, credentials, or `.env` files committed**
- [x] **Prettier + ESLint pass locally** — `format:check` + `lint` repo-wide
- [x] **Tests added/updated** — `tests/utils/pageTitle.test.ts` (25), one case in `e2e/keyboard.spec.ts`
- [ ] **`/code-review` agent review run on this PR**
- [x] **`docs/progress.md` — N/A** for this PR
- [x] **Security implications considered** — titles are fixed strings chosen by path shape; no id, name or other user data is put in the title by this change

## Schema migration?

- [x] No schema change

## Manual test notes

- Unit: one expectation per route declared in `App.tsx` + `admin/routes.tsx`; every route's title is unique; `/suites/new` is not mistaken for `/suites/:id` (pattern order); unknown paths and unknown admin pages are named without throwing; a trailing slash is tolerated.
- Chromium: Dashboard → Results → a run → Back → `/admin/members`. The title follows each step, the run shows its own suite-named title, and Back restores `Results · DataQ`.
- Unit suite 130 files / 1440 tests; a11y (44 scans) + results + smoke green.

## Security / risk notes

Detail routes are titled generically (`Suite`, `Asset`, `Run`) until the page itself knows better; only `RunDetail` does today. Naming the suite/asset in the title is a follow-on for those pages, not a regression.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
